get_list.description: Get one filter list by id, name or its filterlists.com link: the URL to subscribe to and its mirrors, what it blocks, its syntaxes, languages, license and maintainers, the software that can use it, its home page, issue tracker and forum, and the lists it was forked from, includes or depends on. No API key required.

list.description: EasyList is the primary filter list that removes most adverts from international web pages, including unwanted frames, images, and objects. It is the most popular list used by many ad blockers and forms the basis of over a dozen combination and supplementary filter lists.

forks.name: AdGuard Base filter + EasyList (AdGuard for Chromium)

list.name: EasyList

get_list.name: get_list

parameters.description: The list's id, such as 301, its name, such as EasyList, or its page link, such as https://filterlists.com/lists/easylist. A name is matched ignoring case and accents, whole or by its words, but must fit one list; otherwise the step fails naming those it fits.
parameters.name: filter_list

list.description: The list, with where it is published and how it relates to others.

chat_url.description: The list's chat room, or null.

dependents.description: The lists that need this one alongside them to work.

id.description: The related list's id, which Get a filter list takes.

depends_on.description: The lists this one needs alongside it to work.

id.description: The related list's id, which Get a filter list takes.

description.description: What the list does, usually in its maintainers' words, or null when FilterLists has none.

donate_url.description: Where to donate to the list's maintainers, or null.

email_address.description: An email address for the list's maintainers, or null.

forked_from.description: The lists this one was forked from.

id.description: The related list's id, which Get a filter list takes.

forks.description: The lists forked from this one.

id.description: The related list's id, which Get a filter list takes.

home_url.description: The list's home page, or null.

id.description: The list's id, e.g. 301 for EasyList. Get a filter list takes it. Ids only grow, so a higher id is a list added later.

included_in.description: The combined lists that include this one.

id.description: The related list's id, which Get a filter list takes.

includes.description: The lists this one combines, if it combines others.

id.description: The related list's id, which Get a filter list takes.

issues_url.description: The list's issue tracker, or null.

languages.description: The languages of the sites the list is made for. Empty for most lists, which work on sites in any language.

code.description: Its two letter ISO 639-1 code, e.g. 'en'.

id.description: The language's id, e.g. 37.

license.description: The license the list is released under. All Rights Reserved is also what FilterLists records when a list's license is not known.

id.description: The license's id, e.g. 2.

name.description: The license's name, e.g. 'The MIT License'.

permits_commercial_use.description: Whether FilterLists records that it allows commercial use.

permits_modification.description: Whether FilterLists records that it allows changing the list.

email_address.description: An email address for the maintainer, or null.

twitter_handle.description: The maintainer's X (Twitter) handle without the @, or null.

url.description: The maintainer's home page, or null.

onion_url.description: The list's home page on Tor, or null.

page_url.description: The list's page on filterlists.com, with its subscribe buttons, e.g. 'https://filterlists.com/lists/easylist'. Null for the few lists whose name makes the same link as another list's, since the site opens only one list at such a link.

policy_url.description: What the list will and will not block, or null.

software.description: The programs that can use the list: those that read at least one of its syntaxes, as the FilterLists site works it out.

id.description: The program's id, e.g. 1.

submission_url.description: Where to suggest a rule for the list, or null.

syntaxes.description: The syntaxes the list is written in, which decide what can read it.

id.description: The syntax's id, e.g. 3.

name.description: The syntax's name, e.g. 'Adblock Plus' or 'Domains'.

tags.description: What the list blocks or is for, e.g. ads or privacy.

id.description: The tag's id, e.g. 2.

view_url.description: The URL to subscribe to: the list's own file, e.g. 'https://easylist.to/easylist/easylist.txt', or a mirror when FilterLists has only mirrors. A list of DNS resolvers gives the resolver's address instead. Null when FilterLists has no URL for the list. Two lists are split into several files; view_urls has every one.

view_urls.description: Every URL the list is published at, the list's own first and then its mirrors, part by part.

primariness.description: 1 for the list's own URL, 2 and up for mirrors, in the order to try them.

segment.description: Which part of the list it is, from 1. Only lists split into several files have more than one part.

search_lists.description: Search the more than 2,000 filter and host lists in the FilterLists directory by words in their name or description, tag (such as ads, privacy or malware), language, syntax, the software that can use them (such as uBlock Origin or Pi-hole), license or maintainer, a page at a time with the real total. Newest first, with Added after list ID, finds the lists added since a workflow last looked. No API key required.

parameters.description: Only lists added to FilterLists after the list with this id. Ids only grow, so a workflow that runs on a schedule can save the latest list id a search returns and pass it here next time, to hear only about lists added since.
parameters.name: added_after_id

parameters.description: How to order the lists found. Best match, the default, puts a list named exactly as the query first, then lists whose name starts with it, then those whose name holds every word, then those found by their description, each group A to Z; with no query it is A to Z. Name (A to Z) ignores the query, and Newest first puts the most recently added list first.

parameters.description: Which page of results to return, starting at 1. Leave empty for the first page. A page past the last one returns no lists, but still gives the real total.

parameters.description: How many lists a page holds, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20.

description: Find the filter and host lists that ad blockers, DNS blockers and firewalls subscribe to, with the free, open-source FilterLists directory: more than 2,000 lists that block ads, trackers, malware, phishing and annoyances. Search them by words, tag, language, syntax, the software that can use them, license or maintainer, watch for lists added since a workflow last looked, and get a list's subscription URL and mirrors, home page, issue tracker and the lists it forks, includes or depends on. List the tags, languages, syntaxes, software, licenses and maintainers the directory uses too. Every action only reads. No account or API key required.
